title: Why Premium Apps Don't Build Everything Themselves
subtitle: 5 borrowed powers that make your app feel expensive
intro: Your app needs maps, login, emails, chat, and perfect images. Building all five yourself would take months. Premium apps just borrow them.
takeaway: Use specialist APIs for hard features, so you ship a premium feel without building it all.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: the food court, not the solo kitchen
sections.body:
Think of your app as a food court, not one giant kitchen. You run the court, but each stall is a specialist.

An API is a window where you order a job: "give me a map" or "send this email." You don't need to know how their kitchen works.

That division is the whole idea, and the next part shows why it exists.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Buy polish, build your core
sections.body:
Some features need huge expertise to feel premium. Mapbox handles custom maps and live location, Clerk handles logins with polished UI, Resend makes transactional emails land in inboxes.

Stream adds real-time chat and feeds, Cloudinary optimizes images and video via its CDN. You call their API and get that polish in a day.

It feels like a win, but every window you add creates risk, which is next.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When borrowed power breaks
sections.body:
Every API is a dependency - another service you rely on to stay up. If it goes down, your feature goes down too.

Costs, limits, and data rules stack up. Five APIs mean five bills, five outages to watch, and user data flowing to five places.

steps.narration: You keep your core app and borrow hard features via APIs.
Clerk handles login so you don't build auth.
Resend sends the receipt email reliably.
Stream powers chat without you building real-time.
Cloudinary optimizes and delivers images fast via CDN.

quiz.q: What is an API in this food-court analogy?
options: A window to order a specific job from a specialist
quiz.why: An API lets your app ask another service to do one job without knowing its insides.

quiz.q: Why use Clerk or Mapbox instead of building login/maps yourself?
options: They give premium polish and expertise in a day vs months of work
They make your app offline forever
They remove the need for internet
quiz.why: Specialist APIs like Clerk for auth and Mapbox for maps save months and feel polished.

quiz.q: What breaks first if usage grows 100x and you rely on 5 APIs?
options: Bills, rate limits, and outages compound across every dependency
APIs guarantee lower cost at scale
quiz.why: More traffic means more API calls, so costs spike and any outage in one dependency breaks your feature.
